A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GeoRanker and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–K. Text and rendered-page comparisons identify only localized edits on pages 1 and 4; all other pages match.

before.justification: v2 reports original GeoRanker experiments on IM2GPS3K and YFCC4K, including benchmark results, ablations, efficiency analyses and supplementary ranking evaluations.

after.justification: v4 retains the original benchmark results and experimental analyses in Section 4 and the appendices.

M1.justification: The architecture, multi-order distance losses and inference procedure are unchanged. Section 3.2 now explicitly says higher scores correspond to smaller distances, clarifying the convention already established by the loss and maximum-score selection.

E1.justification: Both versions use GeoRanking constructed with MP16-Pro and evaluate on IM2GPS3K and YFCC4K. No datasets, tasks or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Tables 1, 3 and 5, including Random, Top-1 and Prompting in Table 3 and G3 Retrieval in the appendix ranking comparison.

E3.justification: Training settings, candidate counts, geographic error thresholds and experimental controls are unchanged. Appendix F retains the same candidate pool and Recall/NDCG evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The component ablations, hyperparameter analyses, retrieval-pool study, backbone-scale experiments, efficiency analyses and qualitative cases are identical, including their appendix extensions.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals or statistical significance tests.

E6.justification: All reported numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports GeoRanker 1 km accuracy of 18.79% on IM2GPS3K and 32.94% on YFCC4K in both versions; appendix results also match.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(6), distance definitions and loss formulations are identical. The added score-direction explanation restates the ordering already encoded by the mathematics rather than revising a definition or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: GeoRanker, the multi-order distance objective, GeoRanking and claimed state-of-the-art performance on the two benchmarks.

C2.justification: Result interpretations, mechanism arguments and applicability limitations are unchanged. Appendix K retains the same discussion of ranking overhead, potentially skipping ranking and parallel candidate scoring.

D1.justification: Implementation details, LoRA settings, hardware, training times and prompts are unchanged. The code, checkpoint and dataset release statements and access link are also retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and related-work discussion are identical, including positioning against existing geolocalization and learning-to-rank approaches.

P1.justification: Section 3.2 adds the parenthetical clarification that higher scores correspond to smaller distances. The author list changes Yixuan Li to Sharon Li, and the arXiv version/date stamp changes; the remaining prose and document organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: All figures, tables, captions, axes and placements are unchanged. The localized prose and author-line edits do not reorganize the page layout.

improvement.justification: The Section 3.2 clarification reduces ambiguity caused by describing the score as an estimated geographic distance while selecting the highest score in Section 3.4. This modestly improves methodological clarity; the scientific evidence, claims and appendix material remain unchanged.
